name: Divider
summary: A thin line that groups or separates content in lists and layouts. Purely visual, with no label, icon or interactive behaviour; choose it over extra spacing when a boundary must be explicit.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.description: Overrides comp.divider.thickness in dp. Passing a hairline value (1 device pixel) renders a true single-pixel line, thinner than the token default.

anatomy.name: Line
anatomy.description: The only element: a straight line drawn across the full length of its container.

variants.description: Fills the available width at a fixed height equal to thickness.
Fills the available height at a fixed width equal to thickness.
Spans edge-to-edge. Same token group and composable as inset; the difference is purely caller-applied margin.
Indented equally from both ends. There is no dedicated inset token, size or Compose parameter — the caller applies the margin in its own layout.

layout.text: HorizontalDivider and VerticalDivider take no inset or padding parameters of their own; apply any start/end indent through the caller's layout, not a component prop.

HorizontalDivider fills the available width at a fixed height of thickness; VerticalDivider fills the available height at a fixed width of thickness. Orientation is purely which composable is called, not a shared parameter.

behaviour.text: A divider has no interaction states (no hover, focus, press or drag) and no motion; it never animates and never responds to input.

semantics: Not focusable and not exposed to the accessibility tree at all — Compose applies no semantics to it; it is purely decorative and screen readers skip it.

notes.text: MDC-Android also defines a 'heavy' divider style at 8dp thickness; there is no corresponding comp.divider token or Compose variant for it. Implement a heavy divider as a manual thickness override on top of comp.divider.color, not as a distinct token group.
Passing a hairline thickness (Dp.Hairline) renders a true single-device-pixel line regardless of density, thinner than the token default; this is not modeled as its own variant or token.
